title: Yeast Growth and Fluorescence Experiment Using 96-Well Plate Reader
author: Jamie Auxillos
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbicikaw

steps.title: Plan Plate Layout
steps.instruction: Design the layout for both the pre-culture plate and the final 96-well black microtiter plate.

substeps.instruction: For the pre-culture plate, use a checkered pattern by skipping every other row.
For the final plate, organize technical replicates in blocks (which can be set up in different orientations, e.g., upside down).
Ensure the pre-culture plate design corresponds to the final plate for easier pipetting.

steps.title: Prepare Pre-culture Plate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µL of filter-sterilized yeast media (with selection as needed) into each designated well of the pre-culture plate.

substeps.instruction: Dispense media using a multi-channel pipette with a reagent reservoir or a repeat pipette.
Pipette to the bottom of the well to prevent liquid from adhering to the walls.
Seal the plate with a gas-permeable seal.
If outer wells were left empty in the design, fill them with 500 µL of ddH2O.

steps.title: Incubate Pre-cultures
steps.instruction: Grow the cultures overnight in an incubator at 30 °C with shaking at a minimum of 250 rpm to prevent cell pelleting.

steps.title: Dilute Pre-cultures
steps.instruction: After 20 hours, perform a 1:10 dilution of the yeast cultures.

substeps.instruction: Carefully add 900 µL of yeast media to each well containing culture using a P1000 multi-channel pipette (with reagent reservoir) or a repeat pipette.
If using a multi-channel pipette, change tips after each well to avoid cross-contamination.
If using a repeat pipette, dispense to the walls to prevent splashing.

steps.title: Measure OD600
steps.instruction: Determine the optical density of the diluted cultures.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the culture several times using a P100 multi-channel pipette.
Transfer 200 µL of the culture to a clear 96-well microtiter plate.
Measure the OD600 using the plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate Normalization Volumes
steps.instruction: Blank correct the OD measurements by subtracting the OD of the media, then calculate the volume of media needed to normalize the OD to a target (recommended target OD = 0.2).

substeps.instruction: Apply the formula: Volume to add = 800 * ((x - target OD) / target OD), where 800 is the remaining volume in the pre-culture deep well plate and x is the blank-corrected OD.
If the lowest blank-corrected OD is below 0.2, adjust the target OD for the entire plate to match that lowest value.

steps.title: Normalize Culture OD
steps.instruction: Add the calculated volumes of media to the corresponding wells in the pre-culture plate to normalize ODs without rounding the values.

steps.title: Prepare Final Black Microtiter Plate
steps.instruction: Set up the final black microtiter plate for the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of media to the designated blank media wells using a multi-channel pipette.
Gently resuspend the normalized diluted cultures by pipetting up and down several times with a multichannel pipette to ensure cells are not sedimented.
Load 200 µL of diluted culture into each well according to the plate design.
Load one biological replicate at a time, repeating 3x for technical replicates before moving to the next biological replicate.

steps.title: Configure Plate Reader
steps.instruction: Transfer the lidded plate to the Tecan M200 plate reader and configure the 'kinetic cycle' in the Tecan icontrol software.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Corning flat bottom 96 black microtiter plate' and the specific wells to be measured.
Set temperature to 29.9-30.5 °C.
Set kinetic cycle: 80 cycles, linear shaking, 6 mm amplitude at 200-220 rpm, duration of 550 seconds.
Set absorbance measurement: 595 nm, max bandwidth 9 nm, 15 reads.
Configure fluorescence (if needed):
- mCherry: Ex 585 nm, Em 620 nm (Ex BW 9 nm, Em BW 20 nm), Gain 100.
- mTurquoise2: Ex 434 nm, Em 474 nm (Ex BW 9 nm, Em BW 20 nm), Gain 60.
- GFP: Ex 485 nm, Em 535 nm (test gain values 50, 60, or 80 to avoid overflow).
- mTurquoise: Ex 434 nm, Em 474 nm (test gain values 50, 60, or 80 to avoid overflow).
Label the gain values (e.g., 'GFP-80') in the software.

steps.title: Run Experiment and Save Data
steps.instruction: Execute the program and archive the resulting data.

substeps.instruction: Start the program and wait for the plate to heat to ~30 °C and begin shaking.
Verify that the first absorbance and fluorescence measurements are recorded before leaving the run.
Save the raw data file with a sensible name including the date (e.g., 2021-08-10).
Backup the raw data to shared storage and create a separate copy for analysis.
